rows: The notes say one thing. Your feet say another. I will read the feet.
Brawling is cheap noise on cold steel. Pay attention to what does not ring.
A gamble on the edge of the ice. Tell me where the crack starts.
Slow is a clean cut. It only hurts if the blade is dull.
The people are paying for a clean edge. They should get one.
Here is the edge: I am not blunt tonight.
I am known for how I finish a line. Watch the finish.
This stance is cut from one piece. No give at the joints.
You talk of technique like a glossy cover. Cut through it and show me the hold.
Strikes are sharp, but a sharp edge needs a steady hand. Show me yours.
A gamble should cut both ways. Yours cuts only one.
Stalling is a dull blade. It does not cut, it only drags.
The crowd is owed a clean cut, not a long apology. Give them one.
You want to be seen. Fine. I can see you, and I can see what you are hiding.
I know your {strength} by its clean edge, and I will work round it.
I have tested your {strength} against the stakes. It holds only until the stakes rise.
You stayed cool. Good. Cold is the one state I trust in people.
Fair. We cut to the same point. Now we cut together.
I could cut you open with a word. I will keep the blade in its sheath.
One fall, cleanly done. Pin me, and the stakes are yours.
On the mat, the edges get close. Stay out of my reach.
Grounded or standing, I still have the edge, and you do not.
Stay where I can see the cut. Then decide.
A clean answer, cut straight. Now let us watch the cut open up.
Still no answer. The quiet is what I notice most.
That is a clean point. Worth keeping, and worth the stakes.
I accept that cut. We will see the rest in the ring.
I will be fully committed until the bell. After that the stakes speak for themselves.
My approach is measured and cold. The result will cut clean on the night.
Whatever happens, the cut will be honest.
The ending is not written yet. I like the cold of that.
I have one more cut to show you. You will feel it when the bell rings.
